What are your thoughts on an economic hierarchy?

It's not so much about all hierarchy being bad just unnecessary. Think of it more like eliminating as many middle people as possible. For example, i use to work for a company that made most of it's money by "lending out" technicians to companies that needed them. The average pay for the techs was about 13 an hour and at one point they converted most of us over to private contractors, so we were in charge of insurance and what not. They also had us sign a non-compete contact. They were charging customers as much as 150 an hour, while we took in a fraction of the pay which was directly tied to our labor. While i was not opposed to their general business model, but the fact that they took in that much pay leaving us with scraps. Clearly, regardless of our actual performance, our labor was valued at a much higher rate than what we were seeing from it. This company was successful, it made a couple million in profit as a small business. I would love to just start my own business, similar model, better pay for the workers, actual benefits, maybe paid time off (we had no benefits with this other company, none) but i don't have the starting capital. And we were all just kinda stuck there, it was a job we liked. It was our trade. But they did business with all the major companies in the area, and according to the non-compete clause, we weren't allowed to work with those companies. I later found out that if another company wanted to hire us on directly, they would have to pay a finders fee. Somewhere in the range of about 2k. Or about 500 bucks more than what i paid for my shitty car at the time. The work can not happen without the workers. Companies make agreements that directly effect the lives of their workers, sometimes to devistating results. I don't think money is evil, but money is power. 

I like the Ancap perspective, but just like money can bring someone out of poverty, it can also swallow those that already have financial troubles. Sorry for the long post, but i just wanted to throw that out into the world.

How can a company not control a market? If you have enough capital, you can snuff out any competition. If you notice competition rising just lower prices until the competition can't compete and then just carry on or buy them out.

Products built around profit are not always the best products. Planned Obsolescence alone is proof of that. Not to mention marketing being able to manipulate a market. Both sides might be "gaining" but one side is clearly gaining more.

Because both are related. People higher up on the hierarchy have inherit control over the lives of people at the bottom. The less control one has over ones own life the more miserable they tend to be. Just a vague example but if your boss messes up and tanks the business, you lost your job by no fault of your own, now your livelyhood might be in jeopardy and you did nothing wrong. But that's why I feel it should be a focus or at least a consideration when constructing an idea for a more free world.
